title: Every Critic Just Said the Same Word About The Odyssey. The Word Is 'Masterpiece.'
excerpt: The Odyssey premiered in London to the most ecstatic reviews of Nolan's career. One performance drew a comparison to Heath Ledger's Joker — and a British-Indian actor nobody saw coming just became the film's quiet MVP.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Odyssey premiered to unanimous acclaim, marking a high point in Christopher Nolan's career.
  • Matt Damon delivers a career-best performance as Odysseus, with Oscar buzz already surrounding him.
  • Samantha Morton received a standing ovation, a rare honor since Heath Ledger's Joker.
  • Himesh Patel is highlighted as the film's standout, potentially making him a household name.
  • The film features a unique horror sequence, showcasing Nolan's versatility in storytelling.
Critical Acclaim for The Odyssey
›Unanimous rave reviews from critics.
›Compared to Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy.
›Described as a 'crowning cinematic achievement.'
›Critics call it 'the movie to beat' for Best Picture.
Christopher Nolan does not make small films. But even by his standards, **The Odyssey** appears to be something else entirely. https://youtube.com/watch?v=Mzw2ttJD2qQ The film premiered at London's Odeon Luxe Leicester Square on July 6, and within hours, the internet did something it almost never does for a $250 million blockbuster: it agreed. Unanimously. Rapturously. Without hedging. ![The Odyssey — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ea/Fragment_Odyssee_2245_2.jpg) > "Christopher Nolan's #TheOdyssey is an absolute triumph and a crowning cinematic achievement from one of the great filmmakers of our time." — Erik Davis, Fandango > "An astonishing achievement. A triumphant, spectacular epic." — Jazz Tangcay, Variety > **""A career-best powerhouse performance," wrote journalist Simon Thompson."** > "The closest comparison I can think of is Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy." — Jake Kleinman, Polygon That last one is the comparison that should make your pulse quicken. In nearly three decades of filmmaking — from *Memento* to *The Dark Knight* to *Interstellar* to *Oppenheimer* — no one has ever put Nolan in Peter Jackson territory. Until now. **Matt Damon** plays Odysseus, the legendary Greek king trying to get home after the Trojan War, and critics are calling it the performance of his life. "A career-best powerhouse performance," wrote journalist Simon Thompson. IndieWire's Anne Thompson went further, declaring Damon could win Best Actor at the 2027 Oscars and calling the film "the movie to beat" for Best Picture. ![Heath Ledger — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ea/Heath_Ledger_%282%29.jpg) But the real surprise isn't Damon. It's **Samantha Morton** as the witch-goddess Circe. In a July 7 interview with the *Los Angeles Times*, Nolan revealed that Morton was the first actor since **Heath Ledger** to receive a standing ovation from his crew on set. Let that sink in. The last time a Nolan crew reacted that way, they were watching the Joker being born. Morton called the experience "utterly life-changing," telling PEOPLE magazine that working with Nolan at 49 helped her push her craft in ways she never expected. Then there's **Robert Pattinson** as Antinous, the suitor laying siege to Odysseus's wife while the king is lost at sea. "He's so conniving, manipulative, and endlessly entertaining to watch," wrote Erik Davis. "Pattinson leans all the way into the character's villainy." Multiple critics called it one of his finest performances — and this is a man who played Batman.
Standout Performances

**Tom Holland** brings sensitivity and heart as Telemachus, Odysseus's son. *Collider's* Perri Nemiroff singled out his screen presence and chemistry with each co-star, while **Anne Hathaway** as Penelope and **Zendaya** as Athena round out what may be the most stacked ensemble Nolan has ever assembled. ![Peter Jackson — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4a/Peter_Jackson_SDCC_2014.jpg) And here's the detail the Indian press hasn't caught yet: **Himesh Patel**, the British-Indian actor born to Gujarati immigrants in Cambridgeshire, plays Eurylochus, Odysseus's loyal second-in-command. One critic called him, simply, "the MVP." For an actor who broke out in Danny Boyle's *Yesterday* and appeared in Nolan's own *Tenet*, this could be the role that makes him a household name — and the fact that a South Asian actor is being singled out as the standout in a $250 million Hollywood epic is precisely the kind of moment the diaspora should not let slip quietly past. Several critics flagged something nobody expected from a Nolan film: a full horror sequence. "After 25 years, #TheOdyssey gives us a first: a fleshed-out horror sequence directed by Christopher Nolan," wrote *The Hollywood Reporter's* Aaron Couch. The Cyclops. The Sirens. Circe's island. Homer's poem has always been terrifying — and Nolan, it turns out, leaned all the way in. The production is the first film ever shot entirely on IMAX cameras, and critics are begging audiences to see it on the biggest screen they can find. "If you can, SEE IT IN IMAX 70mm," wrote *Collider's* Steven Weintraub. "It's a jaw-dropping experience."
Innovative Filmmaking
›First film shot entirely on IMAX cameras.
›Critics recommend seeing it in IMAX 70mm.
›Features a unique horror sequence.
›Nolan leans into the terrifying aspects of Homer's poem.
**The Odyssey** opens worldwide on **July 17**. In India, it arrives amid unprecedented demand — IMAX 70mm tickets in Mumbai and Pune have sold for ₹3,000 to ₹3,300, the highest ever charged for a film in the country. For diaspora audiences in the US, UK, and Canada, IMAX 70mm screenings are the format every critic is telling you to book. Standard showings will be everywhere. Nine days. The greatest living filmmaker may have just made his masterpiece. Start planning now.
